Activating the Alliance and Transit Pact lets regions propose alliances, share routine upkeep, and fulfill wartime aid requests. Betrayal damages standing and credit limits. New trade orders can choose an escort or a longer detour; existing orders in transit are unchanged. Debt extensions require approval from the largest creditor. Outstanding principal and extension fees must still be repaid with goods available for export.

Debt extensions must be reviewed by the largest creditor, the party holding the largest positive balance. The debtor must have goods available for export, the parties must not be at war, and the breach record must be below 40. A debt can be extended only once per round. If approved, the principal remains, a fee equal to 10% of the reviewing party's share of the debt is added to the balance, and the due date is extended by 600 seconds. Time until due: {变量1} seconds.

Choose route (direct): costs 8 food/1 parts, 300 seconds one way; if the route passes through a third party's war zone at departure, it automatically takes a detour. Escort transport: costs 12 food/3 parts/2 tools, 600 seconds one way. Long detour: costs 20 food/2 parts, 900 seconds one way. The actual buyer pays route fees; a trade pact saves 2 food. No new orders are sent while both parties are under a trade embargo.

If hostilities break out while a direct freight convoy is en route, it will be held in place. If the route remains blocked after 600 seconds, the goods are returned, the balance is reversed, and spent travel costs are non-refundable. Choosing an escort or detour ensures that shipments in transit are delivered, but does not lift a trade embargo between the parties. Each region starts with one unit of public freight capacity. Completing “Expand Public Freight Depot” and maintaining it on schedule adds one more. Changing route preferences does not affect shipments already sent.

A trade pact saves some route food and raises the credit limit by 40. Under a mutual defense pact, when an ally is drawn into an external conflict, you must actually send an aid shipment of 24 grain/4 medicine/4 tools, plus escort fees, within 600 seconds. Both pact types ease bilateral tensions, but each party has limited pact slots and cannot ally with everyone.

If both sides have shortages, they can barter directly. Wartime aid is reassessed every 900 seconds; each arriving aid shipment can support only one round of front-line settlement.
